claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine your Child Benefit eligibility! Let me start by getting the first question from the official assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is your child?** (Please provide their age or birth year)

I need to know this because Child Benefit eligibility depends on the age of the child:
- **Under 16**: Generally automatic qualification (with some exceptions)
- **16-19**: Eligible if they're in full-time education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

Once you tell me your child's age, I'll guide you through the specific eligibility questions for your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me. I'm just wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! So you have one child, **Alex, who is 17 years old** and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17, he falls into the **16-19 age category**. For young people in this age group, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in full-time education or training.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?** 

This could include:
- Full-time school
- Full-time college
- Full-time university
- Full-time apprenticeship or other approved training
- Full-time vocational training

Let me know Alex's current situation, and I'll continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school a while back and hasn't started anything new since then.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has finished school and isn't currently in education or training.

Since he's left education, I need to check if he might still be eligible under the **extension rules**. There's a limited period after someone leaves education where they can still qualify.

**When did Alex finish school?** 

Specifically, how long ago did he leave education? (For example, was it a few weeks ago, a few months ago, or longer?)

This is important because there's a time limit for the extension eligibility after leaving education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the rules that there's a **20-week extension period** after leaving education. This means if Alex left school within the last 20 weeks, he might still qualify.

**Can you tell me approximately when Alex finished school?** For example:
- Was it within the last few weeks?
- A few months ago?
- More than 5 months ago?

This will help me determine if he falls within the eligible extension period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, it's been quite a while now - more than 5 months ago for sure. He left school back in the summer and hasn't done anything since.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex left school in the summer, which means it's now been **more than 5 months** since he left education.

Based on the eligibility rules, the extension period for young people who have left education is **20 weeks** (approximately 4.6 months). Since Alex left more than 5 months ago, he is **outside this extension period**.

Let me navigate through to confirm the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
As expected, the extension eligibility check shows that this extension is **only available if the young person left education within the last 20 weeks**. Since Alex left more than 5 months ago (well beyond the 20-week window), he is **not eligible for this extension**.

Let me navigate to the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
---

## **Assessment Result: INELIGIBLE**

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### **Reason:**

Alex is 17 years old and is not currently in full-time education or training. While there is normally a **20-week extension period** available for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education, this extension has expired in Alex's case. He left school in the summer (more than 5 months ago), which is well beyond the 20-week window.

### **Key Details:**

- The 20-week extension is only available if someone registers with:
  - A government careers service
  - Connexions service
  - Armed services
- Since this extension period has passed and Alex is not in approved education or training, Child Benefit eligibility stops.

### **Next Steps:**

If Alex's situation changes and he enters full-time education or approved training, you would be able to claim Child Benefit again from that point onwards. For the latest information and guidance, you can visit: **https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility**

---

Let me now record this outcome:
